passage.text: Every country has laws to keep people safe.
passage.reading: ˈɛvri ˈkʌntri ˈhæz ˈlɔːz tə ˈkiːp ˈpiːpəl ˈseɪf.

passage.text: But some laws seem strange, or even ridiculous, to visitors.
passage.reading: bʌt sʌm ˈlɔːz ˈsiːm ˈstreɪndʒ, ɔːr ˈiːvən rɪˈdɪkjələs, tə ˈvɪzɪtərz.

passage.text: Here are a few examples from around the world.
passage.reading: ˈhɪr ər ə ˈfjuː ɪɡˈzæmpəlz frəm əˈraʊnd ðə ˈwɜːrld.

passage.text: In Singapore, you can't buy chewing gum.
passage.reading: ɪn ˈsɪŋəpɔːr, juː ˈkænt ˈbaɪ ˈtʃuːɪŋ ˌɡʌm.

passage.text: Selling it has been banned since 1992, because people kept leaving used gum on the streets and on train doors.
passage.reading: ˈsɛlɪŋ ɪt hæz bɪn ˈbænd sɪns ˌnaɪnˈtiːn ˈnaɪnti ˈtuː, bɪˈkɔːz ˈpiːpəl ˈkɛpt ˈliːvɪŋ ˈjuːzd ˈɡʌm ɑːn ðə ˈstriːts ənd ɑːn ˈtreɪn ˈdɔːrz.

passage.text: If you bring a large amount of gum into the country, you can be sent to jail.
passage.reading: ɪf juː ˈbrɪŋ ə ˈlɑːrdʒ əˈmaʊnt əv ˈɡʌm ˈɪntuː ðə ˈkʌntri, juː kən bi ˈsɛnt tə ˈdʒeɪl.

passage.text: Some of Italy's most famous cities have strange rules, too.
passage.reading: sʌm əv ˈɪtəliz ˈmoʊst ˈfeɪməs ˈsɪtiz ˈhæv ˈstreɪndʒ ˈruːlz, ˈtuː.

passage.text: In Venice, it's illegal to feed the birds in St. Mark's Square.
passage.reading: ɪn ˈvɛnɪs, ɪts ɪˈliːɡəl tə ˈfiːd ðə ˈbɜːrdz ɪn ˈseɪnt ˈmɑːrks ˈskwɛr.

passage.text: In Rome, tourists aren't allowed to sit on the Spanish Steps.
passage.reading: ɪn ˈroʊm, ˈtʊrɪsts ˈɑːrnt əˈlaʊd tə ˈsɪt ɑːn ðə ˈspænɪʃ ˈstɛps.

passage.text: If they break these rules, they have to pay a fine.
passage.reading: ɪf ðeɪ ˈbreɪk ðiːz ˈruːlz, ðeɪ ˈhæf tə ˈpeɪ ə ˈfaɪn.

passage.text: Both laws protect old buildings and keep the cities clean.
passage.reading: ˈboʊθ ˈlɔːz prəˈtɛkt ˈoʊld ˈbɪldɪŋz ənd ˈkiːp ðə ˈsɪtiz ˈkliːn.

passage.text: In Germany, it's illegal to run out of gasoline on the highway.
passage.reading: ɪn ˈdʒɜːrməni, ɪts ɪˈliːɡəl tə ˈrʌn ˈaʊt əv ˈɡæsəliːn ɑːn ðə ˈhaɪweɪ.

passage.text: Drivers aren't allowed to stop there unless it's an emergency, and running out of gasoline isn't one.
passage.reading: ˈdraɪvərz ˈɑːrnt əˈlaʊd tə ˈstɑːp ˈðɛr ənˈlɛs ɪts ən ɪˈmɜːrdʒənsi, ənd ˈrʌnɪŋ ˈaʊt əv ˈɡæsəliːn ˈɪzənt ˈwʌn.

passage.text: It sounds ridiculous, but stopping on a very fast road is extremely dangerous.
passage.reading: ɪt ˈsaʊndz rɪˈdɪkjələs, bʌt ˈstɑːpɪŋ ɑːn ə ˈvɛri ˈfæst ˈroʊd ɪz ɪkˈstriːmli ˈdeɪndʒərəs.

passage.text: Some rules seem strange at first, but they are actually very useful.
passage.reading: sʌm ˈruːlz ˈsiːm ˈstreɪndʒ ət ˈfɜːrst, bʌt ðeɪ ər ˈæktʃuəli ˈvɛri ˈjuːsfəl.

passage.text: In 2022, Thailand began to require all passengers in a car to wear a seatbelt, even in the back seat.
passage.reading: ɪn ˈtwɛnti ˈtwɛnti ˈtuː, ˈtaɪlænd bɪˈɡæn tə rɪˈkwaɪər ˈɔːl ˈpæsɪndʒərz ɪn ə ˈkɑːr tə ˈwɛr ə ˈsiːtbɛlt, ˈiːvən ɪn ðə ˈbæk ˈsiːt.

passage.text: Some people complained, but experts say that seatbelts save thousands of lives every year.
passage.reading: sʌm ˈpiːpəl kəmˈpleɪnd, bʌt ˈɛkspɜːrts ˈseɪ ðæt ˈsiːtbɛlts ˈseɪv ˈθaʊzəndz əv ˈlɪvz ˈɛvri ˈjɪr.

passage.text: So before you travel, check the local laws.
passage.reading: soʊ bɪˈfɔːr juː ˈtrævəl, ˈtʃɛk ðə ˈloʊkəl ˈlɔːz.

passage.text: A law that seems ridiculous to you might be very important to the people who live there.
passage.reading: ə ˈlɔː ðæt ˈsiːmz rɪˈdɪkjələs tə juː maɪt bi ˈvɛri ɪmˈpɔːrtənt tə ðə ˈpiːpəl huː ˈlɪv ˈðɛr.
